title: Pair buckets with programmed threshold search

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, n = ceil(log2 N), the single programmed threshold algorithm of proof.md uses the specified fixed stage, packet, cell and search schedules with retained phase rows and their prepared Fourier program registers. It has total charged sequential work T O(2^(n/3) n^2 (log2 n)^2) with that representative and exact growth index 1. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other resource claims and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 7/8 under the fifth claim, including the clean source. All outside constants are absolute.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, n = ceil(log2 N), the single programmed threshold algorithm of proof.md uses the specified fixed stage, packet, cell and search schedules with retained phase rows and their prepared Fourier program registers. It has peak ordinary classical workspace S_C in bits O(n) with that representative and exact growth index 0. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other resource claims and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 7/8 under the fifth claim, including the clean source. All outside constants are absolute.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, n = ceil(log2 N), the single programmed threshold algorithm of proof.md uses the specified fixed stage, packet, cell and search schedules with retained phase rows and their prepared Fourier program registers. It has peak allocated quantum workspace S_Q in qubits O(n^2) with that representative and exact growth index 0. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other resource claims and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 7/8 under the fifth claim, including the clean source. All outside constants are absolute.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, n = ceil(log2 N), the single programmed threshold algorithm of proof.md uses the specified fixed stage, packet, cell and search schedules with retained phase rows and their prepared Fourier program registers. It has total number Q of acquired raw copies, including all discarded and unprocessed copies O(2^(n/3) n) with that representative and exact growth index 1. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other resource claims and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 7/8 under the fifth claim, including the clean source. All outside constants are absolute.

For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, n = ceil(log2 N), the single programmed threshold algorithm of proof.md uses the specified fixed stage, packet, cell and search schedules with retained phase rows and their prepared Fourier program registers. Its proved malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=2^(-20) for every n>=1 under the fixed-position error model in error_model. The total acquisitions are Q = P K 2^B_* with the exact public parameters of proof.md. The full-secret success probability is at least 7/8 for any such joint state and fixed malformed set, including the clean independent source, jointly with all four branchwise resource bounds.

structured.error_model: Among the Q acquired copies, an adversary fixes a set B of at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) malformed positions, possibly depending on N and s. The joint state is arbitrary subject to its reduced state on all other positions being exactly rho_s^{tensor (Q-|B|)}. Malformed systems may be correlated or entangled with each other and with other systems subject to that marginal promise. No source control, purification access, or preparation inverse is supplied.
